current_source_guard.step4_1: 4.1 For $R>0$, the derivative and componentwise FTC in [F6] give $\int_0^R e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}dt=(1-e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)R})/(\gamma-i\omega)$. The modulus formula gives $|e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)R}|=e^{-\gamma R}\to0$ and $|e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}|=e^{-\gamma t}$, whose integral is finite. Thus the stationary covariance is integrable. By evenness, $$S(\omega)=\frac V\pi\operatorname{Re}\int_0^\infty e^{-(\gamma-i\omega)t}dt =\frac V\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac1{\gamma-i\omega} =\frac{V\gamma}{\pi(\gamma^2+\omega^2)}.$$ The integral converges absolutely because $\gamma>0$. [A2, F6, step 3.2]
